summary: A paddock fence of instanced posts carrying three sagging rail courses, parameterised by length_m, post count, height, sag and seed.
objective: At three metres the run reads as a post rhythm with rails dipping between every pair, then chamfered caps and leaning posts, then nail heads and hue jitter.
example_prompts: Run a fence along the lane and around the paddock.
I need a fence I can lengthen without it looking cloned.
not_for: Any claim about stock-proof fencing standards or spacings.
A collider mesh for animal containment: use the returned box collider instead.

silhouette: four posts spaced 1.53 m apart along a 4.6 m run
three rail courses dipping 5.5 cm at the middle of every bay
a chamfered four-sided cap on every post, 10 cm tall
medium: each rail bay built from four chords of the sag curve, not one straight bar
per-post lean of up to 3 degrees off vertical and 9 degrees in plan
rails set 26, 56 and 86 percent of the way up the post
rails nailed to one face of the posts, standing clear of the post line
fine: twenty-four nail domes, 4.2 cm across, a pair at every rail-to-post joint
1.4 cm chamfer on the posts and 1 cm on the rails
per-post hue jitter of 6 percent so no two posts share a tone

principles: A straight rail is the single thing that makes a procedural fence read as a wire diagram. Four chords per bay is enough sag to kill that read.
Posts carry the rhythm; rails carry the line. Jitter the posts and the whole run stops looking cloned even though the rails are identical.
The run ends exactly on its length, so two runs butt together without a double post at the join.
implementation: Call create({ length_m, posts, height, seed, sag }); the run is centred on the origin along X with y = 0 at the ground.
Butt runs together through the start and end sockets; both sit on the run ends, so no post is duplicated.
Posts, caps, rails and nails are four instanced fields, so a hundred metres of fence is still four draw calls per run.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible.
length_m 12 with 10 posts spans at least 7.5 m more than length_m 4 with 4 posts.
Two seeds lean the posts differently while the run keeps its length exactly.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here measures a real fence, its spacing or its stock rating.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at the default four posts over 4.6 m; ten posts over 12 m costs about 5600 triangles. The budget is per default count.
The sag is a parabola, not a catenary: at sag values above about 0.1 m the difference becomes visible against a real rope.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Raise sag and lower height for a rope corral, or set sag to zero and add posts for a stockade.

defaults.rationale: 1.18 m is waist height on a 1.7 m figure, the height at which a fence reads as a boundary rather than as a step, and a short default run keeps the whole fence inside the proof close view where its nails and chamfers can still be counted.
